verdict.tagline: A divine rogue-lite journey blending fluid combat with deep progression.
for_you_if: you appreciate deep tactical weapon combat
you like tackling branching progression paths
not_for_you_if: you dislike extensive grinding for upgrades
you want immediate power gains early on

cohorts.label: 2-20h
cohorts.summary: Early runs blend weapon combat with a magick system while presenting a demanding grind with slow progression.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the game as overly grindy, requiring long-term progress with little immediate payoff or sense of becoming meaningfully stronger during early runs.

citations.review_text:
Ok, so definitely a positive review here, but I can't give it much more than a 7 out of 10.  Incredibly smooth gameplay, great visuals/art design, and interesting story for sure.  And the rougelite structure is sound enough.  My issues with this game, and many like it are these.  1.  Too grindy, and difficult.(if given more accessibility options and modifiers of damage/health, etc. that would be welcome).  2.  No spoiler, but there is an incredibly abtuse section of this game that doesn't really explain how to proceed.  Even with cheats(mods), this game can be frustrating and difficult to get through without guides.  Not great game design.  

That's it.  Other than those two things the game is really nice to have.  Good price too.

I'm 5.5 hours into this game and I don't know why people like it. I've made no meaningful progress towards the main mission, and I never get the items I need to get stronger.  I would enjoy the "failure is still a lesson" model of games if it were possible to not fail.  I want to like the game because of he art, but I've felt zero joy with nothing but failure.  Even God Mode doesn't help you win.  Maybe you will like it, but I reluctantly admit I don't and I regret buying it.

I loved the original Hades, but for whatever reason, Hades II just isn't clicking with me.

The biggest problem is the combat. Melee feels more spammy and much harder to dodge effectively, which pushes me toward relying almost entirely on ranged attacks. But then combat just turns into a different kind of spam fest. Neither approach feels particularly satisfying.

The progression also feels less rewarding. Hades II has what feels like a million different upgrade systems, but none of them seem especially impactful. In Hades I, I remember feeling noticeably more powerful with each run, and that constant sense of growth was a big part of what made the game so addictive.

Eight hours into Hades II, I feel like I'm constantly unlocking things and working toward long-term goals, but very little of it seems to make me meaningfully stronger. There's plenty to progress *toward*, but not much immediate payoff.

And because I'm not enjoying the core combat, that lack of satisfying progression makes everything worse. Runs feel like chores rather than something I'm excited to jump back into.

I can see that a lot of care went into Hades II, and I understand why people love it. I just wish I were having as much fun with it as I did with the original.

Absolute disappointment of a sequel. In Hades I every run was exciting, but this game is not it. Bloated with too many ways to improve the character, and making the game a hell of a grind in the process. Boons are poorly balanced. The screen is more busy than the Shibuya crossing that it's hard to even see the projectiles. The environment keeps getting in the way of your movements. And whoever thought giving the final boss a OHKO attack was a good idea should never develop a game again.

I guess this is what happens when you try too hard to improve on perfect.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game incorporates magic spells and a magick system that blends into the weapon combat.

citations.review_text: This one is so much more fun than the original. It's DEEP, but has by far the best idealization of a combat witch ever written. Melinoë does the cauldron brewing, but it doesn't take over the game, instead it makes for interesting buffs and stages to elevate the story and her abilities. Where OG Hades is like Diablo I and takes you on the same descent everytime, this one is closer to Diablo II and gives you options. The weapons are more fun, the skills are more varied and interesting, and Melinoë is just a charming delight to listen to. And the MUSIC. OMG. Go listen to a YouTube video of "Moonlight Guide Us" So cool.

Hades 2 is a lovely mixture of the old Zagreus combat of using fun melee centered weapons and a new formula of injecting "magick" into the combat system with each weapon giving them each a special flavor of the mixture leaning one way or the other. Also all the characters are awesome and i love them all

single_points.text: One reviewer says that half the boons are complete trash and hurt your kit because they all have some drawback.

citation.review_text:
hyper-lib slop. 

Also, all the keepsakes you get are either useless or hurt you in some way. All the gods have like 5 boons to choose from so you see the same ones over and over. Half the boons are complete trash and hurt your kit (not kidding, they all have some drawback) so sometimes when you get a boon you have to choose the one that hurts you the least. The weapons suck and are just unfun to use.

The game looks great visually but the actual gameplay is lackluster, the first Hades is better and I will go back to playing that.

single_points.text: One reviewer says there is a better way of limiting how far you can get early on without burdening you with a massive debuff every run.

citation.review_text: Pretty good game, but surely there's a better way of limiting how far you can get early on without burdening you with a massive debuff every run? I'd rather you just smack me back to camp than make me keep playing with a debuff. Makes the early part of the game very unfun.

cohorts.label: 20-100h
cohorts.summary: The journey expands through dual routes and branching paths, though later stages demand heavy material grinding.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game includes multiple branching paths for going above and below, which helps prevent the runs from feeling repetitive.

citations.review_text: Hades was the game that got me into rougelikes, this game has definitely satisfied my hunger for more of the story with such lovable and well designed characters. The addition of going above and below options made the game less repetitive and the amount of weapon aspects and builds for each are so fun to explore. I cant recommend this game enough for anyone who is into or trying to get into rougelikes and it is definitely such a treat for the eyes of greek mythology freaks. The only thing I wish to see but couldnt was some of the missing casts from Hades 1 (megaera and thanatos mainly because PLEASE).

Hades II builds on what made the first game so good without changing the combat too much, which I think is a great decision. The biggest improvements are in the playable areas and boss fights. The story also feels more compact, with different branching paths that keep things interesting. My only complaints are the removal of some gods from the first game and the fact that I personally enjoyed the original weapons more. Overall, a great sequel that keeps what worked and adds enough new things to make the experience feel fresh.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features two distinct main progression routes consisting of the Underworld and the Surface.

I didn't like it, but it's a good game

The characters are nowhere near as good as they were in the first game This applies to everyone: the antagonists, protagonists, romance options, and even side characters like Odysseus and Achilles, as well as Hecate and Nyx

Story-wise, it also feels like a step backwards The dialogue isn't nearly as engaging as it was in the first game When you die, you feel less excited about going back and talking to the characters than you did in Hades 1

Overall, the very thing that made Hades 1 so special and innovative feels much less prominent here

However, Hades 2 has made just as much progress in its gameplay and interactive elements as it has regressed in its writing

Unlike the first game, we now have two completely different main routes: the Underworld and the Surface

The boss fights are significantly more engaging than in the first game They have much more varied movesets, greater variety, and better, more distinct arenas This also applies to the miniboss encounters

With the introduction of the Mana system, combat has become more strategic, making the game less prone to devolving into button-mashing

The Arcana Card system and the ability to create builds beyond just Boons add another layer of depth to the gameplay

The game also makes a greater effort than its predecessor to give each region its own distinct identity, resulting in better level design

Enemy variety has also improved considerably

That said, I feel the Boons in the first game were more build-defining and had a more noticeable impact on gameplay I also found the weapons in the first game to be more distinct from one another

The soundtrack, just like in the first game, speaks for itself

However, one thing that really got on my nerves was how unnecessarily drawn-out the whole experience felt The overly long upgrade progression, the punishing difficulty, and the excessive grind required to reach the ending made the game feel like it was stretching things out for…

claims.claim: Reviewers find that late-game progression requires extensive gathering of materials and grinding, which can make completing quests and upgrading weapons feel like diminishing returns.

citations.review_text:
I adore this game, its been a wonderful experience, but at 90 hours i think im done. I feel like I platueaed ages ago after maxing out my grasp, improving my weapons and companions are diminishing returns vs. time spent gathering mats, using the Oath of the Unseen as intended has put the games difficulty outside of my ability. And it feels like there's still so much more to see. 
Such a great game but god im frustrated in a way i never was with the first one.

Weirdly mmo collectathon and so much grinding to get stuff. The game got easier but the bosses have invincibility phases that make the fights pretty boring. Character and story writing are pretty flat and boring hard to care about the plot or any of the characters. Rolled credits and what they do to melinoe's character was a WILD choice. Dont get the 10/10 reviews at all. Spelunky forever.

It's a good game, but it has no business being OP.

It's Hades, for sure. It feels mechanically similar, it has the visuals, the music, the kickass personalities. It's charming and funny, but also moving. It has an enormous amount of top quality voice acting.

So why isn't it as good as the original?

I think it's diluted. The original didn't have half the content of this game, but it also wasn't half as long. This game does everything possible to stretch its content over a shitload of playthroughs. At this point I'm pretty sure I've won more runs than I've lost and yet I'm still trying to find the necessary conversations deep in the RNG to wrap up quests. That... feels like an abuse of my time. 

I deeply enjoyed the first 20 or so hours but now I'm just going through the motions. Some people will love every minute of it, but I'd just like to tie up the loose ends and be done with it. YMMV.

cohorts.label: 100h+
cohorts.summary: Multiple routes continue to break up run monotony over extended play.

claims.claim: The game features multiple routes that unlock to break up the monotony of runs.

citations.review_text:
combat more fun than hades I.
I actually come back to try to clear everything.
good variation in routes (that unlock at perfect times) to take to break up monotony of a run, which hades I didn't have.

I played the first game near when it launched when I was a kid, and finally got a chance to play the second game this year. Man, it's so good.

In many ways I think it's better than the first game. The main thing improved on compared to the first game is variety within runs and incorporating more strategic elements within gameplay. If you've played the first Hades you would know  that while the weapons in it felt fun, alot of the gameplay boiled down to spamming regular and then special attack, and the fun came from testing your twitch reflexes due to the generous i-frame dashes. Melinoe can't dodge nearly as much but she due to her cast you have to play a bit more tactically and slowly. You could say it feels much more balanced. There are dual paths compared to Hades which only has one, so you can switch between routes if it starts feeling monotonous. 
The progression system I think is also well designed and is less rigid and incremental compared to the heat requirements in the first game. However, it can be a bit more slow to get improvements in the beginning since there is more of an emphasis on gathering resources in Hades 2. 

When it comes to the narrative, it can be a hit or miss on how much you like it compared to Hades I. Hades was like lightning caught in a bottle. Much of the fanbase prefered its cast and narrative because it felt more personable/relatable, and Zagreus was charming. Zagreus and his narrative also suits the structure of a roguelike much more naturally as Hades II functions more as a traditional epic. However, I really do think it comes to preference. In my opinion, the Hades I case was much more Zagreus-centric. While the story was more fun and captivating, I felt that the cast of Hades II and their stories felt much more meaningful to me as they operated moreso as individuals beyond Melinoe. The Hades II cast grew on me significantly as a result and I care more for them. The ending of Hades II especially is something that I felt I appreci…

single_points.text: One reviewer says some QOL features are locked behind quite long progression and resource collection.

citation.review_text:
Woman posting review after 100 hours and completing all achievements: It's ok.

So, I beat Hades a few times in Hades 1 and was basically done with it. Didn't gel, either with the mechanics or the story, and I don't particularly like the power-escalation meta-progression or gated story like Hades does.

I still don't in Hades 2. It's actually worse. There are mechanics to hold you back, there are so many unlocks, it takes an age to give you your full toolkit and some QOL features are locked behind quite long progression and resource collection. These are enormous sins. I hate it.

The story is better, for me, personally, than the first game, but I am lukewarm on both. I like a few characters, Melinoe is more interesting than Zagreus, but it's at best fine. The way the story is delivered does not work for me.

HOWEVER... the mechanics in a run absolutely sing. I like the setup, the available tools, the feel of how everything works and the rhythm of the game much much better. The wider builds, the greater variety and ability to spec into different and unexpected aspects of a run's build are very welcome. I enjoy that freedom, flexibility and variety. Which is why I was happy to get so many runs done and then come back and do a whole bunch more after getting the true ending.

Does this help you make up your mind? I have no idea. But I hope you can enjoy it as much as I did (and I will still probably be coming back for more to be honest).

single_points.text: One reviewer says that for the bosses, if they're not phasing in which they're invulnerable, they're either blinking or dashing and if they don't have either they'll have a bullet hell on screen.

citation.review_text:
Great game, if you played hades 1 (which you should) you will most definitely enjoy hades 2 but you'll burn out faster. Hades 2 improves on every aspect of the 1st game but the direction they've chosen with difficulty leaves a bit to be desired. From small arenas to curve balls, the game catches you off guard, especially if you're used to hades 1 with the enemy attack patterns, and the size of each room (save for some biomes) forces you to deal with the... bulls* head on when what you want to do is make some distance to wait for an opportunity to strike, causing you to randomly lose a bunch of hp to some annoying add combination, and when you do have room to maneuver you get bullet hells and melee adds that can completely destroy you if you're not careful.

Now, for the bosses, holy s, if they're not phasing (in which they're invulnerable) they're either blinking or dashing and if they don't have either they'll have a bullet hell on screen, they went a bit too hard on the equivalent of extreme measures (a toggleable option to face a more difficult version of a boss) on this one. Scylla's bullet hell to Chronos attack barrages with little downtime to Prometheus almost non existent telegraphs to the effin special boss spin to the existence of combo breakers and super delayed telegraphs (being Scylla's charge the biggest offender), really hope the sequel (if it's made) has some more consideration with it's difficulty on mid level heat, not just with bosses but with normal encounter adds as well and see what's challenging and what's outright frustrating in their mechanical choices.

I have 250 hours, i did enjoy it but it saddens me to feel so burned out so soon. Ofc i will give it a positive review but i hope Hades 3 improves upon these problems.
